fields.meta_title: Suggestion Form Builder That Answers Every Idea | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a suggestion form that gives every idea a reviewer, a decision date and a written reply, and counts the ideas that ship.
fields.h1: Build a Suggestion Form That Answers Every Idea
fields.hero_description: Describe who sends ideas and who decides on them. Emergent builds the suggestion form and its review queue, then tells each person what was decided and why.
fields.features_heading: Six Parts of a Suggestion Program People Trust
fields.features_subheading: A box on the wall collects ideas and hides what happens next. These parts show each person where their idea stands and why.
fields.feature_1:
Photos and sketches attached to ideas

Let senders attach a photo of the jammed conveyor or a sketch of the new layout. Reviewers see what the sender saw, and every file stays with its idea in your database.
fields.feature_2:
A reviewer and a decision date per idea

Route each category to one reviewer and give every idea a date by which it gets decided. Ideas that pass their date without a decision show as overdue on the review board.
fields.feature_3:
Impact and effort scores

Let a committee rate each idea for impact and effort on a 1-5 scale. Emergent averages the scores into a ranked queue and sends anything above your savings threshold to a manager.
fields.feature_4:
Matching requests merged with a count

Merge entries that ask for the same thing into one request with a running count of people. The count shows real demand, and everyone who asked hears the outcome together.
fields.feature_5:
A written reply for every sender

Email the decision with the reviewer's reason attached, whether the idea was approved or declined. A status page shows where each idea stands without anyone chasing an update.
fields.feature_6:
The app's code in your GitHub repo

Export the full codebase to GitHub on paid plans and host it beside your internal tools. Your developers can change the scoring rules or add a category without waiting on anyone.
fields.why_title: Why Run a Suggestion Program on Emergent?
fields.why_description: Printed slips and template forms stop at submit. A program needs what comes next: a reviewer who decides, and a reply the sender reads.

fields.tab_content_1:
Any idea worth over $5,000 reaches the plant manager

Ana Ruiz runs press 4 at Brightwater Castings. She proposed reusing the foam that inbound parts arrive in, worth $6,400 a year by her estimate. The review committee scored it 4.5 out of 5 at its monthly meeting. Ideas saving over $5,000 also need Dev Patel, the plant manager, who approved it that week.
fields.tab_content_2:
No title request waits for the wrong selector

Pinecrest Public Library takes purchase requests on its website. Each one goes to the selector for that collection: Rosa Kim buys adult fiction and Tom Avery buys for children. A request for The Salt Orchard went to Rosa. Once she ordered it, the patron got an email saying a hold was placed in their name.
fields.tab_content_3:
Early spin made the schedule after 23 requests

The front desk at Ridgeway Fitness keeps a tablet open on the member form, and staff merge matching requests into one entry. By the end of September, 23 members had asked for a 6 a.m. spin class. It starts in November, and each of them got a message with the first class date.
fields.tab_content_4:
Yes to bike racks, and the principal says why

Lakemont High's student council reviews ideas every other Wednesday. Jordan Pike, a sophomore, used her phone to ask for bike racks by the gym. The council sent it to the principal, Ms. Ellison, who approved 12 spaces. Ms. Ellison's written reply gave the reason: 31 students already chain bikes to the fence.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Suggestion Form
fields.howto_description: Decide what happens to an idea after someone presses submit. Then write the questions.
fields.howto_step_1_title: 01 Name a reviewer for each category
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Agree on scoring before any review
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the categories people will suggest in, such as safety or cost, and put one reviewer's name beside each. Pick the day ideas get decided, for example the first Thursday of the month. An idea with no reviewer turns into a note nobody reads.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask what is wrong today, in the sender's own words, before asking what should change. Then ask what the fix would save in hours or dollars. An idea tied to a problem someone can see is far easier to score than a wish.
fields.howto_step_3_des: A name lets the reviewer ask a follow-up question and credit the idea when it ships. Making it optional brings in ideas people are shy about signing. Tell senders plainly on the form what it records about them either way.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Agree on how ideas get scored, such as two ratings out of 5 for impact and effort. Add a threshold that sends large ideas to a manager, for example any saving over $5,000. Print the rules on the form so senders know how ideas are judged.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Tell Emergent the categories and reviewers, plus the reply each sender should get. It sets up the form along with a board reviewers work from and a database behind both. Add a category or change a threshold later by asking for it in one sentence.
fields.howto_step_6_title: 06 Put the form where ideas happen
fields.howto_step_6_des: Pin the link in your team chat and print a QR code for the break room or the front desk. People think of improvements at the moment they hit a problem. The form should be one scan away at that moment.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Answer every idea by its decision date, including the ones you decline, with a one-line reason. Post a monthly list of what was approved and what shipped. Seeing ideas turn into changes is what keeps people sending them.

plan.angle: The live results are issuers' own forms (a YMCA member form, a library purchase request on Qualtrics, a UK research-topic form, a housing association PDF, a fire service's suggestion scheme policy) and a Slack menu-item template; the Semrush top 10 adds SurveyMonkey, Jotform, fomr and Formplus templates and printable slips. They collect an idea and stop at submit, which is why paper suggestion boxes go quiet. This page treats a suggestion form as the front door of a suggestion program: every idea gets a reviewer, a decision date and a written answer, and the ones that ship are counted. It answers the People Also Ask questions on writing and giving a good suggestion and shows four programs: a plant's cost-saving ideas scored by a monthly committee, a library's purchase requests sent to the right selector, gym members' class requests tallied until one makes the schedule, and a high school's student ideas answered by the council.
tab_stories: At Brightwater Castings, a press operator proposes reusing inbound packing foam, the form asks for the problem, the change and a yearly savings estimate of $6,400, and because the estimate is over $5,000 it goes to the plant manager after the monthly review committee scores it.
Pinecrest Public Library patrons request a title they cannot find, each request goes to the selector for that collection, and the patron is told when the book is ordered and placed on hold for them.
Members at Ridgeway Fitness suggest classes and equipment on a form at the front desk, matching requests are grouped, and 23 requests for a 6 a.m. spin class put it on the November schedule.

Students at Lakemont High send ideas from their phones, the student council reviews them every other Wednesday, and a request for bike racks by the gym entrance gets a written answer with the principal's decision.
